text.content:
For a thousand years and more, the warrior caste was the Assamite clan, at least to the rest of the Cainite world. The warriors are the clan's most visibly active caste, historically serving as defenders of the clan and, before the fall of the Second City, as its judges. In the modern nights they have shifted from an overt judicial role to a covert and often mercenary one, and the tradition of the tithe endures: a warrior paid for his services gives a portion to his sire, in honor of the elder who trained and judged him into undeath.

Nickname: Assassins

Caste Disciplines: Celerity, Obfuscate, Quietus

Sect: Roughly one in five warriors belong to the Sabbat (the Assamite antitribu); a similar portion followed al-Ashrad into schismatic alliance with the Camarilla; the remainder are loyal to ur-Shulgi and Alamut, or are dispossessed.

Background: Many warriors come from professions dealing with the application of force — soldiers, police, hitmen, terrorists — but the caste also Embraces noncombatant specialists it finds indispensable: intelligence analysts, smugglers, gunsmiths, strategists.

Character Creation: Physical Attributes are usually a primary concern, though Mental Attributes are valued for strategists and leaders. The caste values Talents and Skills equally; a warrior lacking competence in at least one form of combat is likely a support specialist. Many warriors have Mentors and Contacts. Most schismatic warriors follow Humanity, while loyalist warriors more often follow the Path of Blood; among the antitribu, the Path of Caine and the Path of Honorable Accord predominate.

Loyalist warriors follow standard Assamite organization, operating in packs of two to six members (variously called "fire teams," "squads," "bricks," or "lochos") led by the eldest among them. Each pack answers to a warrior member of the silsila who has a personal connection to, or geographic familiarity with, the pack's leader. Should a new Caliph be chosen, silsila leadership theoretically reverts to that individual, though some members resist the loss of power.

Warriors who follow al-Ashrad are usually subordinate to the eldest magus or vizier in their home city; their vitae addictions and stained auras make them a liability in Camarilla eyes unless properly restrained. Many exist as solitary refugees on the fringes of Camarilla society, though some serve as sheriffs, scourges, or archons. They currently have no formal head, though some favor declaring a "Caliph-in-exile."

The Assamite antitribu maintain their own unique structure within the Sabbat (detailed in the Guide to the Sabbat), historically forming the backbone of the Black Hand.

Bloodlines: The Assamite antitribu consider themselves a separate bloodline, though there is no functional difference from the main body of warriors. A small nomadic North African warrior line of Bedouin stock practices Animalism and makes extensive use of ghoul predators and warhorses; these individuals hold no sectarian allegiance and are only nominally loyal to Alamut.
